clue.text: Way to pay for course

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay for it
a course or route taken

explanation.surface: Someone works out how to pay for a course of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a course of lessons, but here it is a route.
explanation.definitionFit: A footpath is a route for walkers, a kind of way across country.

clue.text: King entering fray causes a shock

indicators.note: something entering another goes inside it

parts.note: a fray is a brawl or fight
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king joining a battle surprises everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A fright is a sudden scare, the same as a shock.

clue.text: Waste year away from Irish county

indicators.note: taking something away from a word removes it

parts.note: Offaly is a county in the Irish midlands
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A year wasted away from home in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the entrails and trimmings of a butchered animal, and by extension refuse or waste.

clue.text: Show clan misinterpreted a form of Langue d'oc

indicators.note: something misinterpreted is read wrongly, so its letters come out in a different order

parts.note: to show something is to prove it
the letters of clan rearranged

explanation.surface: A demonstration that a family group got the old southern French dialect wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Langue d'oc is the group of Romance dialects of southern France, also called Occitan.
explanation.definitionFit: Provencal is the dialect of Provence, one variety of the Occitan language family.

clue.text: For as long as it takes, he'd better not, if worried about it

definitions.text: For as long as it takes

indicators.note: 'about' means placed round, so one part goes around the other
worried words are tugged about, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: these letters to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that he had better not keep fretting over something.
explanation.definitionFit: To the bitter end means persisting right up to the conclusion, however painful, so for as long as needed.

clue.text: Sickness in China? Use antibiotics

indicators.note: 'in' says the letters sit inside the following words, running across the word breaks

parts.note: the letters run across the end of China, all of Use and the start of antibiotics

explanation.surface: Advice to a traveller who falls ill in China: take antibiotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is the queasy feeling of being about to vomit, a form of sickness.

clue.text: Mindful of a conflict over Ecstasy

parts.note: taken as written
a war is an armed conflict
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone conscious of a dispute about drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first parts above the last.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aware is to be conscious or mindful of something.

clue.text: Tranquil silence, in spite of that on Scottish loch

parts.note: still can mean nevertheless or even so
Loch Ness is the Highland loch famed for its monster

explanation.surface: Calm quiet on a Scottish lake despite everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Stillness is a state of calm quiet with no movement or noise.

clue.text: Star in East, twinkling, seen by chance

indicators.note: something twinkling flickers and shifts, so these letters move about

parts.note: the letters of East rearranged
a risk is a chance or gamble

explanation.surface: The Star of Bethlehem twinkling in the East, spotted by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the Nativity star; the definition is the printed symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the star-shaped printing mark, and printers call it a star.

clue.text: Sea dog's steamer

parts.note: surface reading: an old sailor, a sea dog, and his ship
setter's reading: a racing hound of the sea, a fast passenger liner

explanation.surface: An old salt's steamship.
explanation.walkthrough: A sea dog is a veteran sailor, but read literally it is a dog of the sea: the fastest breed of dog afloat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was used for very fast transatlantic passenger liners, likening their speed to racing hounds.

clue.text: Leading elected group of people with a common goal

parts.note: a party voted into power is in

parts.words: group of people with a common goal
parts.note: a front is a political alliance, as in a popular front

explanation.surface: An election report on a winning coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner in front of the field is leading the race; the phrase and the participle are interchangeable.

clue.text: Check on a dazzling display in carriage

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
taken as written
a riot of colour is a dazzling display

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a showy parade of coaches.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle of ancient warfare and racing, a kind of carriage.

clue.text: Own about fifty in Split?

indicators.note: 'about' means going round, so one word is wrapped around the other

parts.note: to own something is to have it
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Owning a place in Split, the Croatian port city, at around fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: Split is capitalised to look like the Croatian city; it is the verb to divide.
explanation.definitionFit: To halve something is to divide or split it into two equal parts.

clue.text: Who lacquers long hair, brushed back? Bank employee, heading off

definitions.note: a clause standing for 'one who lacquers', a noun

indicators.note: hair brushed back is turned the other way, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: a mane is a long head of hair

indicators.note: taking the head off removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: a bank teller serves customers at the counter

explanation.surface: A puzzle about who sprays lacquer on a bank clerk's swept-back long hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Lacquer suggests hairspray, but the definition is someone who applies enamel. The teller loses the T.
explanation.definitionFit: An enameller coats objects with a glossy hard finish, so lacquering is his trade.

clue.text: In a procession classes notice?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: ranks or classes that are marching in a parade
second meaning: dismissal from a job

explanation.surface: School classes noticed walking in a procession.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical literal reading of the phrase; the real sense is being given the sack.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given your marching orders means being told to leave, the same as being given notice of dismissal.

clue.text: Set of rooms beside Thames originally housing soldiers

indicators.note: housing something means giving it a place inside

parts.note: apart in the sense of aside or to one side

indicators.note: what comes originally is at the start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: its opening letter
soldiers in the ranks are men

explanation.surface: Riverside barracks in London where soldiers are quartered.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a flat, a self-contained suite of rooms within a building.

clue.text: Circular and folder in wastepaper basket

parts.note: round means circular in shape
a file is a folder for papers

explanation.surface: A leaflet and a document folder thrown into the bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular' looks like a noun, a leaflet, but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Round file is jocular office slang for the bin, where unwanted papers are filed for good.

clue.text: Sign of wound across one hand cut by this?

definitions.text: Sign of wound across one hand cut by this?

indicators.note: lying across something means stretching over and around it

parts.note: a scar is the mark left by a wound

indicators.note: a word that is cut is shortened, losing its final letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A scarred hand prompts the question: was the blade to blame?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the weapon is the 'this' that might have cut the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved oriental sword, just the blade to leave such a wound.

clue.text: Girl with apple shortly to make dessert

indicators.note: cut short, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a girl's name
a russet is a variety of apple with rough brownish skin

explanation.surface: A girl uses an apple to make a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte russe is a cold pudding of custard or cream set in a mould lined with sponge fingers.

clue.text: Earth flat? Most original of theories

parts.note: plane means flat and level

indicators.note: the most original part is the very start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: The flat-earth idea, the most bizarre of theories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth flat?' suggests flat-earthers; Earth is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is one example of a planet, the third from the sun.

clue.text: Powerful older woman seen in troika, briefly, during parade

indicators.note: something happening during another event sits inside it

parts.note: to parade is to march

indicators.note: a word put briefly is clipped, losing its final letter

parts.note: a troika is a group of three, a triad

explanation.surface: A formidable older woman rides a three-horse sleigh in a parade.
explanation.walkthrough: A troika is a Russian three-horse vehicle, but here it means any trio of three.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is the woman who heads a family or group, typically senior in age and authority.

clue.text: Children's author almost upset dramatist

indicators.note: set upside down in a down clue, the word reads from bottom to top
almost all of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: E. Nesbit wrote The Railway Children

explanation.surface: A writer for young readers is nearly outdone by a playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House, a famous example of a dramatist.

clue.text: Funny turn after onset of dizziness

indicators.note: the onset is the start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter
to roll is to turn over

explanation.surface: A comic routine that ends with someone feeling dizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the turn after the letter in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll means amusing in a dry, whimsical way, a synonym for funny.

clue.text: Invigorating air in heart of blowy region

indicators.note: the heart is the central part, so the middle letter is kept

parts.note: its central letter
a zone is an area or region

explanation.surface: Bracing air found in a windswept part of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is popularly used for fresh, bracing seaside air, as in a tonic breeze.

clue.text: A crime such as this may give one little time to think rationally

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to reason is to think logically

explanation.surface: A capital crime leaves the convict only a short while to reflect before execution.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is grimly apt: treason was once punished by death, which leaves little time to think.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the offence of betraying one's country, a serious crime against the state.

clue.text: Vase containing ornate icon showing fabulous creature

indicators.note: something ornate is elaborately reworked, so these letters are rearranged
one thing containing another holds it inside

parts.note: an urn is a kind of vase
the letters of icon rearranged

explanation.surface: A decorative vase painted with a picture of a mythical beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A unicorn is a legendary horse with one horn, a creature of fable.

clue.text: An ordinary seaman, sailor capsized in front of gondola

indicators.note: a boat that capsizes turns over, so in a down-and-across sense the word turns round

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
taken as written

indicators.note: the front is the first letter only

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A sailor overturned in front of a Venetian gondola.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Royal Navy a rating is a sailor without a commission, an ordinary seaman.

clue.text: Person supporting that woman through a depression

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a word that runs through another lies inside it

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow
pronoun for that woman

explanation.surface: Someone stands by a woman through her depression.
explanation.walkthrough: Depression suggests low mood; it is a dent in a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or backer of a cause or leader, a supporter.
